title: CLO 2025.2 - Knit Editor
description: CLO 2025.2 —— The brand new knit editor is now available. Design your knits freely by adjusting the coil structure and knit thickness, bringing every knitwear idea vividly to life on screen.
transcript:
In this video, I will introduce you to the main feature of version 2025.2, the paper editor, to help you elevate your product design to a new level.  
Now you can directly define the structure of the paper within the 3D project, perform editing, and accurately simulate the shrinkage effect, fully upgrading the design experience.  
Let's take a closer look at the workflow.  

First, select a fabric in the object window.  
In the property editor, change the material type to a wool product.  
In version 2025.2, you will see a new needle ball icon.  
Open the paper editor by clicking on it.  
The paper editor window will appear in the 2D window.  
You can click the option tabs at the bottom to switch views.  
Guiding the draft is very easy.  
You can use a space similar to the 3D window to adjust the draft within the editor.  

Press the middle mouse button and scroll the mouse wheel to align the draft.  
Rotate the middle mouse wheel to zoom in and out of the draft.  
Press and hold the right mouse button and move the mouse to freely rotate the draft around its center.  
Hold the mouse wheel and pinch to make time-catches.  
Use the mouse wheel sandwich to expand the left and right sizes.  
Pinch further to load the entire screen.  

Press the switch button to toggle between any system mode.  
Use shortcut keys to switch to the desired preset view at any time.  

You can use three types of thread line displays to check the paper:  
- Thick thread lines show the actual thickness and solid color.  
- Thin thread lines automatically display the needle structure to enhance visibility.  
- The color of each thread is randomly assigned, so you can easily check the thread structure.  

Next is the core setting.  
Here you can set the size of the paper piece and the final output size.  
To set specific data for the piece of paper, please enter the number of sample cycles in the direction of thread density.  

Then enter the number of sample cycles in the direction of thread density.  
(Repeated phrase in the original text.)  

Now enter the number of sample cycles.  
Then enter the data corresponding to the signal type as shown on the screen in Starburg.  

Next, you can set the line thickness in millimeters and adjust the density of the thread circles.  
Click the icon to see more evidence options.  
The link shows the automatic measurement value of the current result.  
Or you can click to cancel the link.  

Enter the final piece size after shrinkage, such as the number of rows per inch and the thickness of the fabric.  
Change the line thickness.  
The thread circle density adjusts the number of rows per inch.  
After setting the fabric thickness, the real sample will be automatically updated.  

Please note that you do not need to click the reset piece button.  
If you want to understand the definition of any setting, hover the mouse over it to check the tooltips.  

Start editing.  
You can select the needle type from the menu on the right or use shortcut keys.  
Four options are supported, including:  
- Front needle bed, shortcut key Q.  
- Back needle bed, shortcut key W.  
- Front needle bed not edited, shortcut key 1, with the front loop needle as the back line.  
- Back needle bed not edited, shortcut key 2, with the back loop needle as the front line.  

Then you can click and drag the piece to do real needle editing.  

After the sample design is completed, press the simulation button or press the Control key.  
You can use your evidence and custom setting application to simulate the shrinkage effect.  
Now you can see that the piece structure curves due to shrinkage.  
You can continue to edit during the simulation and update the shrinkage effect.  

Press the simulation button or the Control key to pause.  

To apply your piece design to the costume, press the application button.  
Use the result on the 3D costume, or press the application and close to apply the result and close the editor.  

If you want to discard changes, press cancel.  

In the 3D window, you can check the result and make further changes in the editor.  
After changes, press the application button or application and close.  
The editor will add a new one.  

This option is related to the evidence.  
When the paper editor is opened, the thread line is thin.  
The number of rows per inch and the fabric thickness will be used.  
To ensure all changes are managed through the paper editor.  
After closing the paper editor, these options will be available again, allowing you to make further adjustments and immediately check the 3D effect.  

Next, you can adjust the thread line settings in the property editor, such as the color of the thread line and the color of the bone thread.  

After completion, you can save this fabric for future use.  
You can also use the seamless division function for more flexible performance.  

This step-by-step stitch change can now be done using the paper editor to create more accurate and more complex digital piece designs.

chunks.content: ## Introduction to the Paper Editor in CLO 2025.2 This section introduces the new Paper Editor feature in CLO version 2025.2, designed to enhance fabric and product design by allowing direct definition and editing of paper structure within the 3D project. It includes accurate simulation of fabric shrinkage, providing a more realistic and upgraded design experience. The Paper Editor enables designers to define fabric structure, edit the knit pattern in 2D, and simulate shrinkage effects directly within the CLO environment. This integration streamlines the workflow from fabric selection to final 3D application. --- ## Accessing and Navigating the Paper Editor This section explains how to open the Paper Editor and navigate its interface, including mouse controls and view options. - Select a fabric object in the Object Window. - In the Property Editor, change the material type to a wool product. - Click the new needle ball icon to open the Paper Editor. - The Paper Editor opens in the 2D window with option tabs at the bottom to switch views. ### Mouse Controls for Draft Adjustment - Middle mouse button + scroll: Align the draft. - Scroll wheel: Zoom in and out. - Right mouse button + drag: Rotate the draft around its center. - Mouse wheel sandwich (holding mouse wheel): Expand left and right sides. - Pinch gestures: Load entire screen or adjust zoom. ### View Modes and Presets - Switch button toggles between system modes. - Shortcut keys allow quick switching to preset views. --- ## Thread Line Display Types This section covers the three available thread line display modes to analyze fabric structure visually: - **Thick Thread Lines**: Show actual thread thickness and solid colors. - **Thin Thread Lines**: Display needle structure for improved visibility. - **Random Thread Colors**: Assign random colors to different threads for easy differentiation of thread structure. --- ## Core Settings: Paper Size and Sampling This section describes how to configure the fundamental parameters for paper pieces, including size, sampling, and thread density. - Set the paper piece size and final output size. - Enter the number of sample cycles in the direction of thread density. - Input data corresponding to the signal type shown in Starburg (a visualization or measurement tool). - Adjust line thickness (in millimeters) and thread circle density. - Click the icon to view additional evidence options. - An automatic measurement link shows current results, which can be canceled if needed. - Enter the final piece size after shrinkage, including rows per inch and fabric thickness. - Changing line thickness and thread circle density updates rows per inch. - Fabric thickness setting triggers automatic real sample updates. **Note:** There is no need to press the reset piece button. Hover over settings to view tooltips explaining their definitions. --- ## Needle Editing and Thread Type Selection This section details how to edit the knit pattern by selecting needle types and performing direct needle manipulation.
chunks.content_description: CLO 2025.2 —— The brand new knit editor is now available. Design your knits freely by adjusting the coil structure and knit thickness, bringing every knitwear idea vividly to life on screen.

chunks.content: - Enter the final piece size after shrinkage, including rows per inch and fabric thickness. - Changing line thickness and thread circle density updates rows per inch. - Fabric thickness setting triggers automatic real sample updates. **Note:** There is no need to press the reset piece button. Hover over settings to view tooltips explaining their definitions. --- ## Needle Editing and Thread Type Selection This section details how to edit the knit pattern by selecting needle types and performing direct needle manipulation. - Needle types supported (with shortcut keys): - Front needle bed: Q - Back needle bed: W - Front needle bed not edited (front loop needle as back line): 1 - Back needle bed not edited (back loop needle as front line): 2 - Editing method: - Click and drag on the paper piece to edit individual needles. --- ## Shrinkage Simulation and Real-Time Editing This section explains how to simulate fabric shrinkage effects and continue editing during simulation. - Press the simulation button or Control key to start. - The paper piece structure curves realistically to reflect shrinkage. - Editing can continue while simulation is active, with updates applied in real time. - Press the simulation button or Control key again to pause. --- ## Applying and Managing Edited Paper Designs This section covers applying the edited piece to the 3D costume and managing changes. - Press the application button to apply the design to the 3D garment. - Use "application and close" to apply the design and close the Paper Editor. - Press cancel to discard any changes. - Further changes can be made in the Paper Editor after checking results in the 3D window. - After changes, pressing application or application and close adds a new updated piece. --- ## Thread Line Settings and Fabric Saving This section describes additional customization and saving options. - Adjust thread line color and bone thread color in the Property Editor. - Save the fabric with the applied paper design for future use. - Use the seamless division function for more flexible fabric performance. --- ## Summary: Enhanced Digital Piece Design with Paper Editor The Paper Editor in CLO 2025.2 enables step-by-step stitch changes for creating more accurate and complex digital fabric pieces. By integrating paper structure editing, shrinkage simulation, and seamless 3D application, it significantly upgrades the digital knit design workflow.
